result.title: Can Image Generators Hold a Scene Together When Space Is Broken Apart?
result.summary: Image generators are good at drawing scenes in which things that belong together appear next to each other. In almost every image they generate, and in almost every benchmark used to evaluate these images, "belonging to the same whole" and "adjacent to each other" go together. Therefore, we cannot know whether the model truly grasps the scene as a whole, or simply makes each part connect with its adjacent parts. We propose GJBench to disentangle the two. It requires the model to draw a scene as a scattered jigsaw puzzle: an image is cut into interlocking pieces, then moved apart and rotated. Thus, the spatial plausibility of the scene exists only in how these pieces collectively point to a whole. The model may have a reference image, a target layout, both, or neither. We separately evaluate three requirements: whether the scene is broken down into a specified number of separate pieces, whether the pieces interlock, and whether the pieces can reconstruct the reference scene. While every open and closed model we evaluated could draw these scenes well as a whole, none could keep them together as scattered puzzle pieces, and the three requirements categorized failures into different patterns. The models draw separate pieces but miscount them in different ways, and unless their outlines are provided, the pieces rarely interlock, and their content does not reconstruct the reference image. We also found that the target layout helps the puzzle pieces fit together, while the reference image improves neither their count nor their fit. These findings show that keeping a scene continuous across space that the canvas no longer shows remains an open problem for image generators.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GJBench，要求图像生成器把场景画成分散且旋转的拼图块，并分别评测块数、咬合与重建参考场景三项要求，发现现有开放与闭源模型均难以在割裂空间中保持场景整体性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「局部相邻」与「同属一个整体」的解耦思路，可能可供核查 VLM 内部视觉表示是否真正保留全局空间结构而非仅局部连续性；但对象是图像生成器而非 LVR 推理状态，故仅为概念启发。
